  * The level of impact language has on society AND the level of impact society has on language\!
  * Remember sociolinguistics and linguistic anthropology?

---




* __Pop culture __ \(short for “popular culture”\) is a set of practices/beliefs that are dominant in society at a certain point in time
  * That which is transmitted via the mass media and aimed particularly at younger people
  * Changes over time \(what’s popular now is different than what used to be popular\)
  * Can impact how a person views certain topics
  * Is\, by definition\, exclusionary – it cannot include all practices/beliefs; just the most prevalent
  * Can be seen as commercial\, capitalistic
  * Can be seen as being in opposition to “high culture”

# Stereotypes



* A  __stereotype __ is a cognitive structure that includes the beliefs\, preconceived knowledge\, and expectations about a particular social group as held by a particular perceiver
  * It’s about abstract knowledge of what it means to belong to a particular group\, to have a particular set of characteristics
  * Widely held\, fixed\, and oversimplified
* Where do these things come from?

---


# Why do we do this?



* According to cognitive psychologists\, stereotypes are a natural part of human categorization processes
  * __It’s cognitively efficient: __ Once you have the categories\, you can save on processing time by not reconsidering each “member” of a group
  * __It helps us predict our social world: __ We don’t have to worry because you can easily apply your categories to new individuals
  * __It makes us feel good about ourselves: __ We like our own group \(ingroup\) better than other groups \(outgroups\)
  * __It’s automatic?: __ They can even be activated and used without you being aware of it
    * __Subliminal primes __ are stimuli that activate stereotypes without our conscious perception \(subliminal messaging\!\)

---

# An Example: The Lion King

| Good Guys | Bad Guys | Others |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Simba\, Mufasa | Scar\, hyenas | Rafiki\, Zazu |



* _The Lion King_ \, a Disney movie set in Africa\, has good guys\, bad guys\, and others \(like sidekicks\)
* How are they represented?
  * Good guys speak “standard”\, bad guys don’t
  * Others have varying accents

---


| Character | Variety | Character traits |
| :-: | :-: | :-: |
| Simba | “Standard” \(Anglo\) | Strong\, love interest |
| Mufasa | “Standard” \(AA\) | Strong\, noble\, leader |
| Scar | British | Evil\, smart\, effeminate\, snobbish |
| Hyenas | AAE\, Chicano English | Stupid\, lazy\, lowly\, comical |
| Zazu | British | Servant\, authoritative |
| Rafiki | “African” English | All\-knowing \(?\)\, crazy |

Characters\, varieties\, and traits


---


![](images/22-Are%20actors%20good%20at%20dialects_5.jpg)



* Why do they do this?
  * To create an effect\, help us “know” the character
    * Some of the personality is done through the animation
      * Ex\. Scar is smaller than Mufasa\, has a dark mane = not strong but evil
    * But you can build a better character through linguistic stereotypes\!
* Because logically…
  * Why would anyone in the African plains speak with an American or British accent anyway?
  * Why would two brothers have such differing accents?
  * Why would no characters speak an African language?
  * How can you make it palatable to an American audience?

---


# What are the consequences when we use adult stereotypes about voices and social groups to create characters and narratives forconsumption by children?


---




* Disney can decide it wants to have certain voices to give life to their characters\, but the extent to which this is done  _well _ is really on the actor \(and their  __dialect coach__ \, a person who helps actors craft a voice for characters in the context of a production\)
  * Most actors are from a place and can use their native dialect to make the character come to life or the accent is less important to the story
  * Others work very hard at developing a specific accent and often appear in roles using only it
  * Others pick up new dialects for specific productions\, working with a dialect coach to modify the phonetics of their speech
    * Other dialect features would be in the written script
    * Some of these are really good\!
    * And some of these are really bad…

# Who cares?



* Fans\!\!
  * Actors are under increased scrutiny – by native speakers and by people who are very familiar with certain accents – to be as realistic as possible
  * Social media\, the internet\, etc\. = a place to discuss = a place to praise/bash
* Even with fictional places?\!
  * Whatever it is\, it has to be believable\, it has to be relatable\, and it has to bring in money\!
  * Plus\, with the way technology is today\, there is almost no excuse
